items.approach: roundtrip.py: keep the three raw-text presence checks (action verb list, element.name substring, window.title substring) and add a closed-grammar check on a MASKED copy. _mask(text, step): for each non-empty literal in [window.title, element.name, element.control_type, text_summary (type steps)], longest first, blank the FIRST case-insensitive occurrence bounded by non-alphanumerics (re.sub with (?<![A-Za-z0-9])lit(?![A-Za-z0-9]), count=1) -- a manifest literal is authorized only in its one slot, and its words are NEVER added to the allowed vocabulary (this is the fix for Astra's 'Click Delete all records in the Editor window. Delete all records.': the second copy is left unmasked and 'delete','records' are unsupported tokens). Replace the two verb regexes with frozensets _CLICK_WORDS/_TYPE_WORDS (same words). On tokens = re.findall('[a-z0-9]+', masked.lower()): (1) the action check moves here -- a token from the step's own verb set must be present, so an element named 'Click' cannot satisfy it; (2) 'negation' if any token in _NEGATION = {not, no, never, don, dont, avoid, without, mustn, shouldn, cannot}; (3) 'extra_action' if more than one token is in _CLICK_WORDS|_TYPE_WORDS; (4) 'unsupported:<token>' for the first token not in ALLOWED = _STRUCTURAL | _CLICK_WORDS | _TYPE_WORDS | all-digit tokens, where _STRUCTURAL is a fixed set: a an the this that it its your you user in on at to into of from with within inside under for by current here somewhere double right left window dialog screen page button field box textbox checkbox menu item tab link icon option list dropdown panel pane toolbar bar row cell column header label control element position area section form input value text entry. Everything render_step_template emits ('Click the 'X' Button in the 'W' window.', 'the position (412, 233)', '(entered value in field (content not captured))' is masked as text_summary) and every existing stub reply in tests ('Click OK in Test Window.', 'Click the field in Test Window.', 'Click an element in the ... window.', 'The user clicks Save in the SmartDeploy Console window.') stays inside the vocabulary. Return (not mismatches, mismatches); generation.py unchanged (any mismatch -> render_step_template). Add a `# ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling: any non-structural extra word ('carefully') yields the always-correct template, which CLAUDE.md rule 2 allows. F-10 exemption: in server.py _write_all_exports delete the `not verbatim_narration and` guard so round_trip_ok applies to polished step text in BOTH build modes. This is safe: the gate is only ever used to revert to the text that was already shipped (a vision caption or verbatim transcript), never to substitute a template, and a photo step (bare click, empty element/window) can only pass when the rewrite is structural vocabulary, so in practice export polish never rewrites photo step text. Edit phases/DEVIATIONS.md 'audit-fixes F-10' entry: delete the first paragraph (photo-mode skip) and the test reference; keep the second paragraph (claim gate off for no-transcript captures) and append one sentence that those rewrites are now covered by A-01's closed-grammar round_trip_ok.

items.approach: Deterministic source-text grounding: the narrative is accepted only if it is the claims quoted verbatim, in claim order, with at most a closed set of leading connectives; anything else is rejected whole and the stage falls back to the existing [verify] path (no token subsets, no synonyms, no polarity heuristics -- the gate never tries to understand prose). narrative.py: (a) narrative_unsupported(text, claims) -> str | None (public, reused post-polish): drop lines parse_verify_line recognizes; rest = _norm(text) where _norm lowercases and collapses whitespace; keys = [(index, _norm(claim text).rstrip(' .!?'))] for non-empty claims, tried longest first; loop: strip leading whitespace/punctuation (' .,;:!?"\'' and newlines); if some key with index >= last matched index is a prefix of rest and is followed by end-of-text or a non-alphanumeric, consume it and record its index; elif _CONNECTIVE_RE = ^(?:first|then|next|finally|lastly|afterwards|after that|now)\b[,:]?\s* matches, consume it; else return rest[:80] (the unsupported fragment). Return None when nothing is left. This defeats every counterexample on record: 'Copy files from production to backup.' is not a prefix match of 'Copy files from backup to production.'; 'Open settings. Disable all security controls.' leaves 'disable all security controls.'; 'Click Yes.' for claim 'If prompted, click Yes.' is unsupported; 'Disable x' for claim 'Do not disable x' is unsupported; reordering is rejected by the index rule. (b) generate_narrative: after the passes, reason = narrative_unsupported(text, claims); if reason: logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(...) and text = ''; then ensure_claim_coverage(text, claims, placed_text=placed_text) as before -- unplaced claims come out as [verify] blockquotes, placed ones add nothing (so the F-02 failure path and the rejection path are the same path). (c) Prompts carry the claims everywhere: _draft_prompt tells the model to use ONLY the listed sentences verbatim and in order, optionally omitting some or prefixing 'First,'/'Then,'/'Next,'/'Finally,'; _critique_prompt(draft, claims) and _revise_prompt(draft, critique, claims) embed the same bullet list as 'the only permitted sentences' and ask for deviations to be listed / removed. (d) server.py _write_all_exports: after the existing owned/validate_claim_coverage safety net (so its report key and revert still fire first), add: if claims and md_narrative_text and md_narrative_text != narrative_text and (reason := narrative_unsupported(md_narrative_text, claims)): report['polish_rejected_narrative'] = reason; md_narrative_text = narrative_text. Because F-04 always passes claims (synthetic claims = step texts for no-transcript captures), this is the post-polish grounding Astra required for synthetic narratives too. `# ponytail:` comment on narrative_unsupported names the ceiling: free prose from the narrative model is rejected whole; upgrade path is a constrained transformation that preserves predicate arguments, if ever justified. Test stubs: _NarrativeGeneratingStub becomes an echo stub that returns the '- ' bullet lines of whichever prompt it receives, joined with spaces (grounded by construction, works for passes=3).
